flashcards.q: The three pricing anchors for any AI feature?
flashcards.a: COGS floor per user (module-06 arithmetic incl. usage skew), value ceiling vs the buyer's real alternative (task-hours x loaded rate, tickets deflected), and market anchors ($30/user/mo Copilot enterprise precedent; ~$20 consumer-chat-era prosumer anchor).

flashcards.q: Why did unlimited-usage AI pricing die and what replaced it?
flashcards.a: Per-request variable costs met power-user skew (P99 users consume 10-50x median) making flat prices negative-margin; unlimited tiers retracted within quarters in 2023-2024. Replacement: hybrid seat covering ~P80 usage plus metered credits at 3-5x marginal COGS, caps on pathological paths.

flashcards.q: What does 'positioning is choosing your judge' mean?
flashcards.a: Market category determines the comparison set: positioned as software you're judged cheap/fast/flawless; as labor replacement, against fault-tolerant humans at salary-scale prices. AI loses most labor comparisons on reliability - position at TASK level ('first drafts in minutes'), never person-replacement.

flashcards.q: Cite two documented stats on GenAI pilot failure.
flashcards.a: Gartner projected ~30% of generative-AI projects abandoned after proof-of-concept by end of 2025; MIT's 2025 NANDA study reported ~95% of enterprise GenAI pilots showing zero measurable P&L impact. Causes are mostly organizational, not model quality.

flashcards.q: Name the six killers of AI features.
flashcards.a: (1) Undefined outcome - no baseline/success spec; (2) no evals - quality claims untestable; (3) unit economics - unlimited inference meets power users; (4) trust/compliance stalls - PII/hallucination exposure; (5) workflow non-integration - feature lives in its own tab; (6) ownership ambiguity - nobody owns the P&L.

When attribution is clean and verifiable by both parties: per-resolution support AI, per-screened-candidate recruiting, per-document pipelines. Explodes when outcomes lag months or depend on many inputs - attribution disputes become billing disputes. Fallback: price measurable proxies or stay on seats/consumption.

flashcards.q: What's wrong with 'add AI, charge $30/user like Microsoft'?
flashcards.a: Copilot's $30 rides M365's installed base, IT distribution, and deep workflow embedment - the price reflects that moat. Copying the number without embeddedness produces sticker-shock churn because users compare against free consumer chatbots. Cite it as category validation, not your number.

flashcards.q: Van Westendorp method: four questions and cautions?
flashcards.a: At what price: too cheap to trust / a bargain / expensive but considerable / too expensive? Intersections give acceptable band + indifference point. Cautions: 100+ real buyers per segment, describe offer concretely first, watch anchoring on consumer-chat prices, report segments separately (power users skew means).

flashcards.q: Users try the AI feature twice and vanish. Diagnose.
flashcards.a: Killer #5: workflow non-integration - activation without habit. Check time-to-first-value (>2 min = dead), 7-day return cohorts, entry-point analysis. Fix: embed at the moment of need (in-editor/in-ticket/in-doc), zero invocation friction, measure depth-of-use not trials. If embedding reveals weak VALUE, back to discovery.

flashcards.q: Add-on SKU or bundled tier for AI - how do you choose?
flashcards.a: Add-on when costs are material/variable, WTP segments differ sharply, ROI visibility needed. Bundle when AI is table-stakes parity (charging invites switching) or premium-tier mix-shift beats standalone revenue. Watch the ratchet: bundling raises COGS forever with flat pricing power; add-ons can later be bundled as sweeteners, rarely reverse.

flashcards.q: What makes 'wrapper' accusations stick and what escapes them?
flashcards.a: Sticks when supplier can replicate you in one release cycle, switching costs nil, COGS tracks supplier whims. Escapes: proprietary data loops with measured outcome improvement, workflow embedment (months to rebuild), eval/compliance depth in regulated niches, distribution. All four are strategy-module moats - the wrapper question IS the moat question.

flashcards.q: Sketch the path-to-GA doc for a support-ticket AI pilot.
flashcards.a: One page naming each killer + owner: outcome spec (deflection baseline/target, CSAT floor); golden-set evals (~500 tickets) wired into CI with human-parity threshold; COGS/resolution ceiling vs $5-15 ticket benchmark + cascade architecture; PII redaction, low-confidence human-review queue, audit logs; agent-console embedding; named PM+eng pair with weekly decision log. Kill conditions upfront.
